2_Introduction: The target PSCs achieved an average power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.2547% with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 23.034 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.9989 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 61.9526%. 1.5 mol/L Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 perovskite precursors were prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 4700 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second spin-coating step, 200 µL of antisolvent was introduced at last 8 s. Then, the film was annealed at 115 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite film—governed by the delicate interplay among A-site cation mixing (Cs⁺ enhancing phase stability and suppressing δ-phase formation while FA⁺ maintains optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.91), B-site Pb²⁺ lattice rigidity, and X-site halide composition (Br⁻ incorporation widening the bandgap slightly and reducing halide vacancy formation energy)—is critically modulated by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol: the initial low-speed step (1000 rpm, 10 s) enables uniform precursor wetting and early nucleation, whereas the high-speed step (4700 rpm, 30 s) imposes strong shear forces that accelerate solvent evaporation and promote rapid supersaturation; crucially, the precisely timed antisolvent quenching at the final 8 s of the second step triggers instantaneous nucleation across the entire film, suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding a dense, pinhole-free morphology with large, oriented grains—as corroborated by high-coverage grayscale intensity maps and uniform PL emission across optical micrographs—while the 115 °C/30 min thermal annealing drives complete solvent removal, facilitates Br⁻/I⁻ homogenization, relieves residual tensile strain (evidenced by narrowed XRD (110) peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ at 12.6°), and promotes thermodynamically favored α-phase crystallinity, collectively minimizing deep-level trap states at grain boundaries and surfaces. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the synergistic stabilization conferred by Cs⁺ doping—reducing A-site volatility and ion migration—and Br⁻ alloying—suppressing iodide interstitials and lowering the formation energy of Vₐₛ defects—while the optimized crystallization kinetics inherently limit non-radiative recombination pathways, as directly evidenced by spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and prolonged average carrier lifetime in time-resolved PL mapping, which jointly reflect suppressed trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination and efficient radiative extraction. VOC = 0.9989 V, JSC = 23.034 mA/cm², FF = 61.9526%, PCE = 14.2547%.
